The wallet's unshieldProtocolFee mirror is asserted against these same rows
in wallet/tests/a7_exit_fee_mirror.test.ts. The two implementations are
therefore compared against ONE table, not against each other's arithmetic —
two implementations that happen to agree are not evidence.
REGENERATED at lane A6.6 from a real canister run, at the parameters ruled
unshield_flat_minimum = 2.5 STSH (was 0.1 STSH). The crossover — where the
two arms of max() coincide — therefore moves from 40 STSH to 1,000 STSH,
which is exactly the floor rung of the A6.6 five-tier denomination ladder:
the flat minimum binds only BELOW the ladder, and the bps arm governs every
rung on it. Because the fee is integer floor division, one e8s above the
crossover the floor STILL binds; 100_000_000_400 e8s is the first amount
whose bps fee strictly exceeds it (400 e8s of amount buys 1 e8s of fee at
25 bps). The final row is the largest exit that fits the widened circuit
